questions.question: In the demo's controlled experiment, what was the direct cause of the fixed chunking missing half the answer?
options: The fixed-window chunks were too large, diluting semantics
The answer sentence straddled the boundary of chunks 441/442 and was cut in half
The embedding model was not frozen for the fixed chunking
The fixed chunks carried no metadata
questions.explanation: See the "Fixed windows and structural splitting" section: the same question misses half its answer under fixed chunking (the sentence straddles chunks 441/442) and hits whole under structural chunking.

questions.question: Why does the lesson insist tables and code must stay whole chunks?
options: Tables and code are the largest in token count, so splitting wastes window
A table cut in half loses its row-column correspondence; cut code loses syntactic and logical integrity
Tables and code cannot be encoded by an embedding model
Keeping them whole halves the number of chunks
questions.explanation: See the "Tables and code are special chunks" section: a table cut in half loses its row-column correspondence, and cut code loses syntactic and logical integrity — a retrieved snippet will not even compile.

questions.question: Which is NOT a post-recall value of "metadata travels with the chunk"?
options: Provenance after recall — citations and audits depend on it
Filtered search, e.g. "only policies updated in 2026"
Metadata participates in the similarity computation and raises the score
Disambiguation, e.g. section context distinguishing "breach" in different sections
questions.explanation: See the "Metadata travels with the chunk" section: metadata does not alter the similarity computation, yet it earns its keep in provenance, filtered search, and disambiguation.
